description: Lets the portfolio's own artefacts merge themselves on green, short of a major: every Maven coordinate and Gradle plugin under `io.github.youndie` (and the old `ru.workinprogress.sborka` plugin ids). Extend it AFTER the base preset, next to `automerge-harness`: `"extends": ["github>youndie/sborka", "github>youndie/sborka:automerge-harness", "github>youndie/sborka:automerge-own"]`.

Why it exists: the queue that keeps filling is not the harness. On 2026-11-25, 90 Renovate pull requests were open across youndie/*, 83 of them green; 41 were the portfolio's own artefacts and 22 of those were ONE sborka publish (0.5.0.135 → 0.5.0.136) opened in every consumer. Ten repositories sat at the five-pull-request limit with green pull requests that nobody was going to read: a bump of a library this portfolio wrote, built and tested in its own repository, and then built again by the consumer's own pull request.

The argument is the harness one, one step further. A bump of our own library is not a decision the consumer makes — the decision was the change in the library, and that had its review there. What the consumer can add is its build, and the pull request already ran it. A head bump that changes a verdict (a new kapkan rule, an API that moved) turns the consumer's pull request red, and a red pull request does not merge itself: it waits for a person, as now.

A MAJOR still waits for a person, and so does anything that is not on Maven under these groups — the images (`ghcr.io/youndie/*`) a stand or a chart names, and sborka's own actions, which are harness and belong to `automerge-harness`.

THE PRECONDITION IS TWO-FOLD, AND NEITHER HALF IS RHETORICAL. First the harness one: a pull request has to run the build — look at what runs on `pull_request` in the workflow, not in a sentence about it. Second: a merge to `main` must not ship anything to people by itself. Where `main` deploys a production service (mani), a library bump that merges itself is a release nobody decided on. A stand that deploys from `main` is the owner's call per repository; this preset does not make it. sborka itself does not extend this: every merge there publishes a new version and re-opens a bump in every consumer.

`verifyOwnPreset` in sborka's `check` fails if a rule here that sets `automerge` could reach a major, a coordinate outside the portfolio, or skip the pull request's checks — and if the patterns stop matching the portfolio's own names, because a rule that matches nothing reads exactly like one that works.

packageRules.description: The portfolio's own Maven artefacts and Gradle plugins merge themselves on green, short of a major: their review was in their own repository, and the consumer's pull request has already run the consumer's build.
